V1: Is the suspected leak/invalid free real, or a false positive / benign report?
R2: What does the tool's report category or runtime error mean (definitely/indirectly/possibly lost, still reachable, suppressed, invalid pointer)?
R3: Is the report caused by my code, or by a library, runtime, or the tool itself?
R4: Where was the block allocated / where does the leak or bad free originate?
R5: How do I detect, configure, or suppress this with the tool?
A1: Is this memory on the heap at all (vs. stack, static, string literal)?
A2: Does this function/API allocate what it returns (must the caller free it)?
A3: Which allocator family produced this pointer (malloc/new/new[]/custom/library)?
A4: Is the allocation size bounded and validated (untrusted input, overflow, huge/negative size, failure)?
O1: Who is responsible for releasing this memory (caller vs. callee contract)?
O2: Was ownership transferred (to a container, smart pointer, library, or object), so someone else releases it?
D1: Is there a matching release for this allocation, and where should it go?
D2: Is the pointer passed to free exactly the one the allocator returned (not offset/advanced)?
D3: Is the deallocator the right one for the allocator (free vs delete vs delete[] vs library free)?
D4: Is the pointer valid to free right now (initialized, not already freed, not dangling)?
C1: Is the memory released on every path: error handling, early return, exceptions, longjmp?
C2: Is the old block released on each loop iteration / reallocation (realloc failure, reassignment in a loop)?
L1: Must the memory be freed before program exit, or is exit-time retention acceptable?
L2: Is the object destroyed when its lifetime ends (scope exit, destructor called, virtual destructor)?
L3: Does memory keep growing with repetitions (retained longer than needed, unbounded growth)?
L4: Are threads joined/detached so that their resources are released?
E1: Was the last reference overwritten or lost before release?
E2: Does the pointer escape (global, struct field, return value) so it must be released elsewhere?
E3: Do other aliases or copies refer to the same block (shallow copy, copy ctor, two owners)?
N1: Are nested sub-allocations released (struct members, list nodes, 2-D arrays) before/with the parent?
N2: Is a reference cycle or refcount imbalance preventing release?
N3: Does the cleanup routine / destructor release every resource the object owns?
X1: Are allocation and release done by the same module/runtime heap (DLL, CRT, FFI boundary)?
G: Generic: why does this leak/crash? (no specific evidence asked)
T1: Triage: reproducer, full trace, version, build flags
K: Allocator internals (how free knows the size, etc.)
RK: What kind of resource is held (memory, fd, socket, handle, JNI ref, GPU object, thread), and which call releases it?
R6: Is the growth in RSS / task-manager memory leaked memory, or freed memory the allocator has not returned (fragmentation, arenas, caches)?
D5: Is the block accessed after it was released (use after free, dangling reference)?
H1: Was the heap already corrupted before the failing free/malloc (earlier overflow)?
